_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-19 · SkyFetch (Session 170) — the three new MAP Custom Reports are live on the API we already pull, two are wired into the nightly job, and Pedro has confirmed both the student-ID scrambling and that its secret does not change. Ashley's Delta items are unchanged and still open.
_status:
Sam built three new reports in MAP's Custom Report Builder and asked whether we could fetch them and check them against what we already store. We can — all three are served by the same MAP address the nightly job has been pulling from for months, and the row counts the API returns match the builder screen exactly. So this was a settings change, not a new piece of plumbing, which also means we can politely decline ITPI's offer to push the data to us daily: we already fetch it ourselves, and doing the fetching is what lets us choose which columns we take.

The bigger surprise: two of the three reports are OUR OWN request coming back. The 13-field one is exactly the dataset we wrote out and sent to MAP's team on 9 August — same columns, same order — and we already hold a copy of it. So the real job was never 'get the data', it was 'check whether their numbers and ours agree'. They very nearly do: MAP's counts are 1.5%, 3% and 10% higher than ours, all in the same direction, which is what we expected — our copy is slightly stale because MAP has been correcting and reloading records. That is our data catching up, not an error to chase.

On privacy: the student report identifies people only by a scrambled code. Pedro confirmed those codes are properly scrambled with a secret, and we checked independently rather than just taking his word — we tried five million guesses against a sample code and none matched. Pedro has since confirmed that secret stays the same each night, so student counts ARE comparable week to week. Sam has also told him the tables are wired into our nightly job, so ITPI does not need to push anything to us — that question is closed.

Nothing is loaded into our database yet. That is the next session's job.

items.text: Ashley is meeting San Joaquin Delta College with a list of 42 occupations where the college already teaches the content and the MAP credit recommendation already exists. Worth knowing how it lands — and if Delta corrects any of our matches, those corrections are the most useful thing to come back with, because they tell us where our course-matching was wrong.

Delta teaches a utility/hydroelectric apprenticeship — turbines, protective relaying, high-voltage switching, aqueduct systems — covering 6 jobs with NO credit recommendation anywhere in California. The question to ask the college is who sponsors that apprenticeship, because that sponsor is who any new MAP exhibit would be built around. This would be first in the state.

Delta runs a full 10-course plumbing apprenticeship, but it is filed under no plumbing-named program, so it does not show up in a program search and MAP does not know Delta has it — the statewide plumbing contractor exhibit lists Delta on neither side. Worth asking the college directly whether other pathways are hidden the same way.

Delta has no fire technology instruction at all, and fire is the biggest block on the SJCOE list (17 occupations) and the best-covered in the state. So those students either get referred elsewhere — Modesto has the largest career portfolio in California — or Delta decides to build a fire program. That is a decision for the meeting, not something we can fix.

Three decisions still open on splitting the public site from the internal one, all from Session 169 and none of them urgent: does the public Knowledge Base stay CC BY 4.0 (it currently lets anyone reuse the methodology commercially — the highest-leverage of the three); are we on GitHub Free or Team (Free cannot publish a site from a private repo, so it decides what is possible); and does the CPL-Initiative GitHub organisation have a second owner yet? Pedro was added on Supabase but GitHub was never confirmed.

Still outstanding after three sessions: run a SECOND partner's occupation list through the statewide crosswalk engine and work whatever it cannot match. Until that happens, the claim that coverage builds up across partners is a design intention rather than something we have shown.

After Ashley's Delta meeting, record which of the 42 the college accepted, rejected or corrected into kb/delta_offering_map.json. The corrections are the highest-value input — they are the only signal that tells us where our judgment about a course was wrong.

First job next session: confirm the two newly-wired MAP reports actually arrived on the nightly run (the fetch now pulls 10 datasets instead of 8). A silent miss would look exactly like nothing changing.

Load the two new reports into Supabase and compare them against what we already hold, college by college. Start with Moreno Valley — it spans 8 catalog years where most colleges have 5, so it tests the part that actually matters. Expect their numbers to be slightly higher than ours; that is our copy catching up.

Pedro confirmed the scrambling secret for student IDs stays the same each night, so student counts ARE comparable over time. Still build the check that would spot it changing later — compare this pull's set of student codes against last pull's — because if it ever did change, nothing would show an error; the numbers would just quietly stop matching.
CLAUDE.md is twice the size it should be (120KB against a 60KB budget) and every session pays that cost on startup. Move a chunk of prose into docs/reference/ — do not add more to it.
